verifiable-quality-gates.why: the whole PR makes the discrimination-test step provably real: pinning each gate's test CONTENT (testSha256) so a hollowed always-pass test is caught by parity, provenance and integrity, not merely that a test file exists (#123) - directly the 'a check that passes but might not be catching anything' case
verifiable-quality-gates.what: added testSha256 to the schema + manifest (11 gates) + the three gate scripts; 8 ISSUE-123 discrimination cases across 4 test files; integrity exit 0, full suite 750 pass, 0 fail, 3 skipped
quotes: test must FAIL when the check is replaced by a no-op

architectural-decision-records.why: adding testSha256 to the manifest contract and to three gate scripts is architecturally significant and recorded in one ADR
architectural-decision-records.what: wrote ADR-0080 covering the schema/manifest/three-script change and the honest limits (pins byte-equality not discriminating-power; gates only, not machinery; schema-optional but enforced at source/release)
quotes: Every architecturally significant change ships with an ADR in the same unit of work

comprehensive-test-strategy.why: pinned at the layer that owns each check: fixture-based tests that run the real parity/provenance/integrity gates against manifests with matching, drifted, missing and dropped testSha256, plus the schema validator
comprehensive-test-strategy.what: fixture tests for hollowed-test, dropped-testSha256, missing-testSha256, and matching cases
quotes: Test at the lowest level that can catch the bug, and match the test type to the risk.

bdd-comprehensive-testing.why: the non-happy paths were enumerated and committed: a hollowed test, a dropped testSha256 vs a release that pins one, a missing testSha256 at the source, and a wrong testSha256
bdd-comprehensive-testing.what: node:test cases across parity/provenance/integrity/schema asserting the real exit code for each
quotes: These are not optional and not left to judgment.

skeptical-audit.why: ADR-0080 states the honest limit rather than overclaiming: testSha256 pins byte-equality to the released test, it does NOT re-prove the test is discriminating (that is the mutation gate's job, not a hash)
skeptical-audit.what: recorded the limit in ADR-0080 and verified integrity + the full suite green before claiming the fix
quotes: If you cannot attach all three, you do not assert it

judge-arch.why: a fresh-context review was run on the testSha256 delta before the PR, checking the three gates' comparisons, the LF-normalized hashing, and that the schema/manifest stay consistent
judge-arch.what: ran judge-arch in a fresh subagent and recorded it in the arch-review log
quotes: These are not optional and not left to discretion. Every review does all of them.

owasp-secure-coding-bdd.why: the testSha256 pinning is supply-chain/CI integrity (a copied test cannot be hollowed undetected), covered here by verifiable-quality-gates; no product input/auth/crypto/upload surface changed that would take an @security Gherkin scenario

pattern-selector.why: no new feature, class, module or data flow; adds a hash field to the existing manifest contract and a comparison to the existing gates

arch-encode.why: enforced by discrimination tests and the manifest contract, not a new rules-file entry

compliance-data-lifecycle.why: no PII, retention, migration, backup or audit logic; this is gate/manifest integrity

enterprise-architecture-standards.why: no system, service, database or integration architecture changed

release-deployment-safety.why: no deploy, migration, feature-flag or rollback mechanism; the manifest contract change ships in the 1.3.1 line, covered by provenance, not a release-safety mechanism

sre-operational-readiness.why: no SLI/SLO, alert, runbook or production-operability surface

universal-accessibility-wcag.why: no user-facing or UI surface; CI/gate tooling

universal-browser-device-support.why: no browser or frontend code; CI/gate tooling

usability-ux-universal-design.why: no user-facing flow, screen, form or copy; CI/gate tooling
